To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have performed single-neutron knockout experiments with intermediate energy beams of Mg-30,Ma-32 and that we report on a first observation of intruder states in the ground states and a direct comparison of spectroscopic factors with shell-model predictions.

we have observed a dramatic change in the single-neutron knockout cross section from Mg-32 compared with Mg-30, which is a direct indication of the change from the N=20 shell gap to the N=14 shell gap.

we observed the breakdown of the N = 20 shell-closure for the first time in the ground state of Mg-32, and we observed a dramatic change of the single-particle structure between the two ground states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the evolution of single-particle levels in the island of inversion, and the transition between normal and intruder configurations.
the evolution of nuclear structure as a function of the number of protons and neutrons in nuclei far from stability, in particular the breakdown of the N = 20 magic number in nuclei around Mg-32.
the structure of the very neutron-rich nuclei Mg-30 and 32 and with the evolution of single-particle structure as a function of neutron number.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ground-state wave functions of Mg-32 and Mg-30 are dominated by the intruder configurations.
the N=20 shell gap is strongly broken, and that Mg-32 lies in the transitional region between normal and intruder-dominated states.
the ground state of Mg-32 is indeed an almost pure 2p- 2h state, with only a small admixture of 1p-1h configurations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N=20 shell gap has indeed collapsed for Mg-32, while it is still present for Mg-30, in agreement with shell-model calculations.
we have observed a dramatic change in the single-particle structure between the two isotopes.
the N=20 subshell is broken in both Mg-30 and -32, but the ground state of Mg-32 has a much larger intruder component than Mg-30.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N=20 shell closure is strongly broken in the ground state of Mg-32.
the ground state of Mg-32 is dominated by 2p- 2h N= 20 cross-shell configurations, as predicted by the large-scale shell-model calculation.
we have observed the first intruder-dominated ground state in a neutron-rich nucleus beyond the drip lines.
